engine_1.name: Cryptographic Identity Engine
features_implemented: Local Elliptic Curve Key Generation (Ed25519) via Android Keystore on first boot
SHA-256 Hashing with URL-Safe Base64 encoding for compact public keys
Masked User Identifier Generation prefixed with 'void_'
Closed internal storage input/output secure stream bindings

engine_2.name: Multi-Hop Mesh Routing Matrix
features_implemented: Stateful dynamic ad-hoc network routing tables
Standalone MeshPacket structures with Ed25519 cryptographic signatures
Automated Time-to-Live (TTL) ceiling set at 64 hops to prevent network loops
Autonomous background packet forwarding protocol for remote peers
Adaptive Link-Layer Routing: Primary via Wi-Fi Aware (NAN), with automated background BLE Beacon fallback for hardware fragmentation

engine_3.name: VoidDrop Air-Gapped Share Pipeline
features_implemented: Custom Layer-4 Byte Stream routing directly into network interface buffers (wlan0/p2p0)
Bypass of Android High-Level Media Frameworks and System Logging Networks
Zero-compression, high-bandwidth local frequency data streaming
Zero-Log metadata management (No cloud logs, no OS-level tracking history)

required_permissions: allow voidos_daemon self:rawip_socket { create read write };
SELinux_Policy.status: Policy mapped to prevent build-time permission denial blockades

components: Notification Bar Pull-down Window Manager Hooks
Volume Slider / Hardware Key Broadcast Receivers

architectural_statement: VoidOS rejects centralized corporate identities, DNS protocols, and cloud dependencies. The backend daemon runs autonomously at system level under a custom SELinux domain, transforming independent physical hardware into local infrastructure.
